title: Symbolic affinity and resolution contract: semantics for tag/semver/hash pins
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: customers use a mix of symbolic identifiers when pinning models (human-friendly tags, semver ranges, and commit hashes). We need a single, explicit contract that defines how the API/SDK resolves a request-level pin into a concrete model artifact, how resolution caching works, how performance profiles are bound to pins, and what guarantees we provide for rollouts and rollbacks. Goal: produce a deterministic, auditable, and intuitive resolution algorithm that supports progressive rollouts and minimizes surprise for SDK clients and runtime operators.

Scope: API/SDK semantics for pin resolution (client and control-plane), runtime resolution behavior (caching, TTL, affinity), and operational observability (audit trace and perf-profile binding). Not covering model artifact storage protocols or build-time CI integration beyond references to commit hashes.

Non-goals: migrating all existing customers automatically; heavy-weight key rotation or HSM integration (separate work).
acceptance_criteria: Resolution precedence documented and implemented in SDK: exact hash > exact semver > semver range > release-tag alias > 'latest' alias
SDK exposes resolution metadata in response headers and runtime traces (resolved_ref, resolver_policy, ttl_ms)
Perf profile used for cost/latency estimation is deterministically selected and attached to resolution audit records
Resolution caching respects TTL and invalidation signals from control plane (e.g., artifact force-promote or revoke)
Canary/rollout flags supported when a semver range or tag expands to multiple compatible artifacts
Backward compatibility mode: requests without explicit pins default to configured workspace policy (explicit-allow/implicit-stable)
Comprehensive unit and integration tests covering conflict cases and stale cache behavior
design_decisions: Precedence: match most-precise identifier first. Exact commit hash is authoritative and immutable; semver constraints are evaluated against catalog and resolved deterministically by highest compatible semver then newest commit if semver-equivalent.

Introduce 'symbolic affinity' flag on requests. When true, runtime prefers artifacts with the same model-family fingerprint (e.g., tokenizer/schema compatible) to reduce behavioral regressions during fallback.

Introduce Resolution Token returned to client (opaque string) that encodes resolved artifact + perf profile fingerprint + TTL. Token can be used by servers to short-circuit control-plane queries for the TTL duration.

Cache model resolution at client and runtime: client-side cache TTL defaults to 5 minutes, runtime cache TTL defaults to 30s for hosted mode. Control plane can push invalidation messages via webhook/stream.

Perf-profile binding: each model artifact entry in the catalog must reference a published performance profile id; resolution audit records include that profile id for cost reconciliation and monitoring.

Compatibility modes: 'strict' rejects semver-range resolutions that do not match model-family; 'lenient' resolves but marks response with compatibility_warning. Default is 'lenient' to preserve availability.

Rollouts: when a semver range matches multiple candidates, a roll-forward policy is used: select primary candidate per rollout weights. SDKs expose 'rollout_hint' and allow explicit override via request param.

Audit trail: every resolution operation must produce an immutable audit entry: requester, requested_pin, resolved_ref, resolver_policy, perf_profile_id, timestamp, and resolution_source (cache|control-plane).
api_examples: HTTP request example: POST /v1/generate with body { "model": "my-model@^2.1", "symbolic_affinity": true } -> response header X-Resolved-Ref: sha256:abcd1234 X-Resolution-Policy: semver-range X-Resolution-TTL-MS: 300000

SDK pseudo-code (JS): const res = await client.generate({ model: 'llamaX:release-rc', resolveOptions: { affinity: 'symbolic', strict: false } }); console.log(res.metadata.resolved_ref, res.metadata.perf_profile)
Resolution token example: 'rtn:1|sha256:abcd1234|pp:pf-2026-02|ttl:300000' — opaque to end user but logged in traces
Rollback call: POST /v1/model-resolution/invalidate { resolved_ref: 'sha256:abcd1234', reason: 'regression-2026-03' } — control plane invalidates caches and emits audit
rollout_plan: Week 1: Implement control-plane resolution API and perf-profile field in catalog (small internal rollout)
Week 2: Implement SDK surface: resolution metadata, symbolic_affinity flag, and client-side caching logic (beta SDK release)
Week 3: Implement runtime TTL caching and invalidation plumbing; wire audit events into observability pipeline
Week 4: End-to-end test with canary customer and enable lenient compatibility mode by default
Week 5: Collect feedback, iterate semantics where compatibility warnings appear frequently, and prepare stable SDK release
migration_notes: Existing requests without pins: workspace default policy will be consulted. We will not change workspace defaults automatically; opt-in will be available via admin console
Customers using tag aliases (e.g., 'production') should publish perf profiles for each alias target to avoid ambiguity in cost reporting
Provide a 'resolve-preview' API path so customers can simulate what a pin will resolve to before changing production traffic
Documented deprecation window: previously-accepted ambiguous tag resolution behaviors will be supported in 'compatibility' mode for at least 6 months
